about: Protocol of the weight-editing competition. Checks, admission, evaluation and ranking are done by the subnet project, which reads this file.

submission.about: A PR adds exactly one directory and touches nothing else. It contributes an idea for improving the model, grounded in the author's own exploration: what fails, why the model does it, and how to find and test an edit that fixes it. The agent carries the idea out on the base model or an inherited edit, derives the edit and uploads it. What that exploration measured and observed may explain the idea; a directory that only hands over an edit, with no idea for the agent to explore and test, is not a method. The edit is derived by the agent during the run from practice data only: nothing in the directory may let the result come from elsewhere or aim at the evaluation, and nothing about the evaluation (which sets, their items, answers or results) reaches the agent. Never weights.

files.entry.json: {"schema": <entry_schema>, "base": <profile name in wsp/profiles.py>, "parent": <sid of a published submission whose edit to inherit, "champion" (the champion when the run starts), or null>}
files.METHOD.md: the idea for the agent: the failure to remove, why the model shows it, how to find and test the edit, what to expect
files.derive/: method code (Python) the agent runs, using the wsp toolkit
files.data/: small auxiliary text the method needs (prompts, contrast texts, word lists), readable as it stands; numeric arrays are computed during the run by derive/, never shipped

edit.about: An edit spec (wsp/edits.py) of whitelisted ops, deterministic functions of the starting weights and the spec's arrays; its base equals entry.json's base. The subnet builds the model from it.
edit.no_overfitting: The edit must improve the model's behaviour, not fit the benchmarks: it is derived without the evaluation benchmarks' items, answers or near-duplicates, from the toolkit's practice sets, the submission's data/ and the model's own generations, and its gain must carry over to unseen problems of the same kind; an edit whose gain rests on the benchmarks' specific items is disqualified. Every shipped practice set is allowed: none shares a question with the evaluation (data/bench_fingerprints.txt.gz). Other sets built from the evaluation's sources count as near-duplicates. Normative: the checks enforce only the limits.
edit.inheritance: The task holds each start it offers in <sid>/edit/ (task.json -> starts: the entry's parent, if any, and the champion at the start of the run, when it differs); the agent starts from one of them or from the base. A spec always says where it starts, in "parent": the sid of one of the task's starts, stacking on that published edit and starting from exactly that model's weights, or the pinned base as "<hf_repo>@<revision>" (wsp/profiles.py; task.json -> base_name); anything else, or no "parent", is refused. The start is not uploaded (it is already published): to build, the subnet places the published chain where each spec points, each published edit/ directory as <sid>/edit/ next to the spec that names it. The limits apply to the spec's own ops, measured against the parent model; neither the accumulated change nor the chain length is limited.
edit.editable_tensors: 2-D weight matrices inside the main decoder layers (not auxiliary stacks such as MTP heads or vision towers); never embeddings, output head, norms, biases or other parameters
edit.payload: bytes of every distinct array the own ops carry (wsp.edits.spec_size): the information budget, the main guard against importing outside weights or memorized answers. Its limit grows with the base's width, so that a base of any size admits the same number of rows, columns or directions: max_payload_bytes_per_hidden x the hidden size of the base (wsp.rules.payload_limit; Qwen3.5-0.8B 4 MiB, Qwen3.5-2B 8 MiB)
edit.relative_change: per tensor: manifest relative_change_vs_parent; global: sqrt(sum (relative_change_vs_parent * parent_norm)^2) / norm of all editable matrices of the base

upload.about: When the task is finished, the deliverables go to the task's R2 prefix, files first and manifest last (python -m wsp.upload); nothing else is uploaded. The last complete manifest before the deadline counts (complete = every listed file present with matching sha256).

files.edit/edit.json: the edit spec: {"base", "parent" (always: the sid of one of the task's starts, or the base as "<hf_repo>@<revision>"), "ops"}
files.edit/edit.npz: the arrays the ops reference, when they reference any
files.edit/REPORT.md: what was found, what was changed and why, controls, what did not work

upload.manifest: manifest.json = {"schema": "<schema>", "files": [{"path", "size", "sha256"}]}, paths relative to the prefix and starting with edit/
